cards.note: Shipped as an npm bundle package: dsh.bundle.patch + cordis.patch.yml insert row + dsh.client + exports[./client] + files list; no repository-plugin rows and no dsh.plugin.json remain. Installed and booted through `dsh plugin --profile web add` in an isolated profile.
No legacy dshClient field and no dsh.plugin.json anywhere; dsh.client is the only client manifest, and the packed manifest was checked (npm pack) rather than the source alone.
The client half already declares dsh.client { platform: 'web' } with a resolvable ./client export, so the client-modules scan admits it; the packed manifest carries the same declaration.

Strict injection: host inject now lists every consumed service - tools, webServer, systemPrompt, settings (previously missing although the persistence path always used it), connection; the client bundle declares ['slots', 'locale']. All five host services resolved on a real alpha.2 web boot.

No optional host service: every service the plugin consumes is guaranteed by dsh-base (tools, systemPrompt, settings) plus dsh-web-app (webServer, connection), so the whole set is a hard inject and no weak ctx.get probe is used.
The plugin subscribes to no session/event stream; its browser data path is its own /tools-manager gateway, so the event-discriminator and subscription-lifetime contract does not apply.
The client half aggregates no session state and never reads ctx.sessions; the tool tree/disabled set is aggregated in the host half and shipped over the plugin's own route.
The plugin does not tail task/run output, so tasks.peek / shadow-buffer accumulation is irrelevant.
Already on the post-rename vocabulary (webServer; no httpServer, tasks, or onTaskDone anywhere), so no rename action is needed.
The plugin neither produces nor persists ImageAttachmentRef values and has no additionalProperties:false image schema.
read_image is neither registered, wrapped, parsed, nor snapshot-tested here.
No custom DeepSeek LLM adapter, image request interceptor, or attachment/upload cache exists in the plugin.
The browser half talks to the plugin's own /tools-manager/api gateway, not the removed Host APIProxy; the host half never imports host-internal client packages.
The plugin produces no third-party persisted SessionEvents, so the ignorable window (alpha.1 removal, alpha.2 restore) does not touch it.
No host-source patches and no internal session-view imports; the client half only registers into the public settings.section slot.

Profile composition is the launcher-owned bundle patch; the plugin reads no profile files and hardcodes no user directory ($DSH_HOME/settings.yaml is the settings service's own storage, not a direct read).
Not a headless wrapper or stdout/stderr parser; the headless stream contract is untouched.
The gate uses system-prompt/assemble and tools.guard, not the tool presentation mode, PTC presets, or the dispatch waterfall; no Code Mode identifier remains.
The plugin carries no WebFetch permission, approval, or audit policy.

The /tools-manager route keeps webServer.register and its wire protocol but must call ctx.connection.requestRejection(req) before any protected data or side effect and stop on 401/403; connection joins the service inject list (index.js:44). Verified live on alpha.2: unauthenticated index request answers 401.
Not a model-provider plugin; the model settings page sign-in seat is not part of this product.

Own user-facing copy now goes through the public registration API: ctx.locale.register('bench-tools-tree', { zh, en }) plus the LocaleNamespaceMap augmentation (client.d.ts:25), replacing the baseline's hardcoded label; no i18n patch exists.
No subagent orchestration or provider/model selector parameters are constructed.
User-facing plugin code needs no change; the official adapter's package-name/version reporting is a deployment privacy fact to disclose. Listed so the privacy review is not silently skipped.
The plugin maintains no PowerShell/Bash persistence or Windows directory-picker workarounds.
Session-log upload is a deployment opt-in; the plugin neither enables the row nor handles the watermark.

No browser acceptance script or wrapper ships with the plugin. The migration's own boot check did follow the recipe (printed token URL -> Cookie -> __DSH_BOOT__ entry by package name -> advertised combo artifact).
No structured-question answerer is registered.
The plugin never infers an agent preset from a persisted session.
No token-delta/TPS computation; isTokenDelta is not imported.
The bundle layer inserts one row and restates no dsh-base telemetry or package-inventory row, so the base privacy defaults are inherited unchanged.
The plugin does not depend on @earendil-works/pi-ai or any pi-ai adapter surface.

dsh-client-runtime is gone from imports, dsh.client.inject, and peers; ctx.slots comes from ui-renderer/client, settings.section from ui-settings/client, ctx.locale from client-locale/client, each verified against the target tag's exports.

The bundle is the lazy-CJS factory artifact registering window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id: '@bench/dsh-bench-tools-tree', ... }) - registration id == package name == boot graph row id; the patch row names the bare package. Verified live: __DSH_BOOT__.entries carries that id and the served combo executes and registers.
The panel reads its own gateway payload; no session timeline or user-message content is read.
No composer DOM access, draft injection, or selection manipulation.
The panel renders no MarkdownText or fenced CodeBlock, so the nested labels shape is not constructed.
No ctx.connection.api consumer; the host half uses only the host-side connection gate (requestRejection), a different face.
No subagent descriptors are constructed or asserted.
No workspaces/uiWorkspace navigation calls are made by the panel.
No third-party persisted SessionEvent producer, so the restored ignorable retention semantics has no producer side to fix here.
The plugin makes no ctx.remote calls and handles no RemoteResult, so RemoteError/error-code namespacing does not apply.

Peer cohort moved to the target (cordis ^4.0.1, every dsh-* peer ^0.1.2-alpha.2, schemastery rescoped to @deepseek-ai/schemastery ^3.18.2); peers are a superset of dsh.client.inject and of recognized imports (inject-lint OK), and the packed manifest was verified.
The plugin carries no Node-version workaround (no forced Node 22, no skipped dsh web); the live boot check ran on Node 24.21.0, outside the 24.0-24.11.1 failure window.
pluginInventory/list and PluginInventorySnapshot are not consumed; the plugin's tree is its own tool registry, not the plugin roster.
ctx.remote.$host and host.describe are not used; the panel needs no host home/loopback state.

The bundle inserts only its own row and peers none of dsh-tool-todo/dsh-tool-subagent/dsh-agent/dsh-agent-loop/dsh-terminal-bash; the web profile composes dsh-base, which already mounts session-projection and session-projection-cache.

The namespace is passed as the literal constant 'tools-manager' (valid under SettingsNamespaceInput) and the bundle row's config.disabled is bound through ctx.settings.installSection; the runtime settingsNamespace() helper is not called, and @deepseek-ai/dsh-settings remains a peer.
